title: Rigid automations decay into “zombie apps” within months unless domain experts maintain and evolve them as models advance
text: Interviewees across 58 companies repeatedly described top-down custom chatbots and vendor-built point solutions decaying into unused “zombie apps” as underlying models leapfrogged them—sometimes within three months—leaving teams feeling like they were “trying to throw darts at a spinning dart board,” or leaving managers ignoring customer-service scores generated by a two-year-old model. By contrast, durable agentic workflows required active post-launch expert ownership: one engineer who automated production-alert triage read every agent transcript for two months to fix prompts, integrations and missing vendor docs, continued biweekly transcript sampling six months later, and evolved the agent into company-wide infrastructure.
qualification: Qualitative observations across 66 interviews at 58 US Anthropic customers during a period of rapid quarterly frontier-model releases; exact obsolescence rates vary by task stability and integration depth.

public_locator.value: It’ll be obsolete in three months.
